stem: A client presents in an emotional crisis but has no immediate medical instability. What should the nurse prioritize early in crisis intervention?

options.A: Complete a comprehensive lifetime psychiatric history before asking about immediate safety concerns.
options.B: Assess immediate safety and urgent needs, use calm supportive listening to understand the crisis, and connect the client with appropriate crisis resources.
options.C: Begin long-term psychotherapy goals before identifying the immediate problem that precipitated the crisis.
options.D: Encourage the client to manage the crisis independently before assessing available supports or urgent risk.

rationale: Current SAMHSA 988 guidance describes early crisis support as beginning with safety assessment, followed by listening to understand how the problem is affecting the person, providing judgment-free support, and sharing or connecting the person with helpful resources. The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan likewise places crisis intervention in Psychosocial Integrity and includes assessing potential violence/safety, identifying the client in crisis, using crisis-intervention techniques, and guiding the client to recovery resources. Therefore B is the priority. A delays immediate safety assessment, C moves prematurely to long-term treatment goals, and D withholds needed assessment and support during an active crisis.
educational_objective: Prioritize immediate safety assessment, supportive therapeutic listening, identification of urgent needs, and connection to appropriate resources during early crisis intervention before comprehensive history-taking or long-term treatment planning.
source_organization: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
source_version_date: Current SAMHSA 988 FAQ live-rechecked August 16, 2026; page content current in 2026 with no separate clinical-version identifier displayed
source_locator: FAQ sections describing what happens during a 988 call/chat/text: counselor asks about safety, listens and works to understand how the problem is affecting the person, provides personal/judgment-free support, and shares resources or community connections as needed.
source_claim_supported: Early crisis support prioritizes safety assessment, understanding the immediate problem through supportive listening, and connection to appropriate resources rather than delaying for comprehensive history or long-term treatment planning.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.31 > Crisis Intervention: assess potential for violence and use safety precautions; identify the client in crisis; use crisis-intervention techniques to assist coping; guide the client to resources for recovery from crisis. Psychosocial Integrity activity statements also include therapeutic communication and assessment of support systems.
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — crisis intervention, safety, therapeutic communication, and resource connection

source_original.rationale: Early crisis intervention prioritizes immediate safety and urgent needs, active listening and understanding of the crisis, support, coping resources, and connection to appropriate services. SAMHSA's 988 model explicitly begins with safety assessment, listening, support, and resource connection. The keyed response is correct.
source_original.source_detail: SAMHSA describes crisis counselors as first asking about safety, listening to understand how the problem is affecting the person, providing judgment-free support, and sharing helpful resources. Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, coping, cultural/spiritual influences and psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the early-crisis-intervention construct and key B. Tightened B to mirror the current SAMHSA sequence of safety assessment, supportive listening/understanding, and resource connection, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct prioritization principle supported by both SAMHSA and NCSBN.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current SAMHSA 988 crisis-support guidance; official NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: SAMHSA 988 FAQ live-rechecked 2026-08-16; NCSBN 2026 RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31
audit_findings.exact_locator: SAMHSA 988 FAQ call/chat/text flow; NCSBN Psychosocial Integrity printed p.31 > Crisis Intervention
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses only directly supported early-crisis priorities: safety, immediate understanding/support, and connection to resources. It does not claim that 988 workflow is the only permissible nursing protocol and does not defer safety for comprehensive history-taking.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because immediate safety/urgent needs precede a comprehensive lifetime history during an active crisis.
distractor_audit.B: Correct and directly supported by SAMHSA and NCSBN crisis-intervention principles.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because long-term psychotherapy goals do not precede identification and stabilization of the immediate crisis.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because an active crisis warrants assessment of risk, supports, and urgent needs rather than unsupported independent management.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B includes the source-supported early sequence without delaying safety assessment or moving prematurely to long-term planning.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe plausible ordering choices during crisis care; the key is determined by priority and safety, not by a unique jargon cue.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity — Crisis Intervention, therapeutic communication, support systems, and safety precautions.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-audited the current SAMHSA 988 FAQ, NCSBN 2026 Psychosocial Integrity/Crisis Intervention text, stem, all four alternatives, rationale, objective, difficulty, ambiguity, cueing, and scope. B remained uniquely correct with no unresolved conflict.
